parsed.claim: The Lean quantity velocityC1Norm can be ⊤ even though the spatial supremum of the derivative operator norm is at most 1. For the identity field on ℝ³, ‖v‖_∞ = ⊤ makes velocityC1Norm = ⊤ while sup‖∇v‖ ≤ 1. So velocityC1Norm = ⊤ does not by itself force the gradient to be unbounded. The Gagliardo–Nirenberg step with the energy bound would be needed.
parsed.lean:
theorem probe_C1_discrepancy :
    Euler.velocityC1Norm (id : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3) → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)) = ⊤ ∧
    (⨆ x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3),
      ENNReal.ofReal ‖fderiv ℝ (id : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3) → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)) x‖) ≤ 1 := by
  constructor
  · have h : (⨆ x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3), ENNReal.ofReal ‖(id x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3))‖) = ⊤ := by
      refine ENNReal.eq_top_of_forall_nnreal_le fun r => ?_
      refine le_iSup_of_le (EuclideanSpace.single 0 (r:ℝ)) ?_
      simp [EuclideanSpace.norm_single, ENNReal.ofReal_coe_nnreal]
    unfold Euler.velocityC1Norm
    rw [h]
    simp
  · refine iSup_le fun x => ?_
    rw [fderiv_id]
    exact ENNReal.ofReal_le_one.mpr ContinuousLinearMap.norm_id_le
